## PCI PM callbacks reaching `i915_pm_suspend`

The relevant PCI PM dispatch chain is:

```text
pci_pm_suspend()
  └─ pm->suspend(dev)                 // drivers/pci/pci-driver.c:851–855
       └─ i915_pm_suspend(kdev)       // drivers/gpu/drm/i915/i915_driver.c:1392
            ├─ kdev_to_i915(kdev)
            ├─ checks switch_power_state
            └─ i915_drm_suspend(&i915->drm)  // :1404
                 └─ intel_display_driver_suspend(display) // :1120
                      └─ drm_atomic_helper_suspend(display->drm)
```

And for hibernation/poweroff:

```text
pci_pm_poweroff()
  └─ pm->poweroff(dev)                // drivers/pci/pci-driver.c:1189–1193
       └─ i915_pm_suspend(kdev)
            └─ i915_drm_suspend(&i915->drm)
                 └─ intel_display_driver_suspend(display)
                      └─ drm_atomic_helper_suspend(display->drm)
```

The i915 `dev_pm_ops` wiring assigns `i915_pm_suspend` to the system suspend and poweroff paths; codegraph reports the dynamic links:

- `pci_pm_suspend → i915_pm_suspend`
- `pci_pm_poweroff → i915_pm_suspend`

Within the i915 callback, the common portion is:

```c
static int i915_pm_suspend(struct device *kdev)
{
        struct drm_i915_private *i915 = kdev_to_i915(kdev);

        if (!i915)
                return -ENODEV;

        if (i915->drm.switch_power_state == DRM_SWITCH_POWER_OFF)
                return 0;

        return i915_drm_suspend(&i915->drm);
}
```

Source: `drivers/gpu/drm/i915/i915_driver.c:1392–1405`.

### Callers that also call `i915_pm_runtime_suspend`

None of the callers reaching `i915_pm_suspend` also call `i915_pm_runtime_suspend`.

Specifically:

- `pci_pm_suspend()` calls the generic `pm_runtime_resume(dev)` when required, but not `i915_pm_runtime_suspend()`.
- `pci_pm_poweroff()` likewise calls generic `pm_runtime_resume(dev)`, but not `i915_pm_runtime_suspend()`.
- `i915_pm_suspend()` itself does not call `i915_pm_runtime_suspend()`.

Thus there is no caller overlap between the `i915_pm_suspend` chain and an `i915_pm_runtime_suspend` call.

## `dev_priv` data flow to `intel_display_suspend`

The symbol is named `intel_display_driver_suspend` in the indexed source:

```text
i915_pm_suspend(kdev)
  └─ i915 = kdev_to_i915(kdev)
       type: struct drm_i915_private *
       value: driver-private data recovered from struct device
  └─ i915_drm_suspend(&i915->drm)
       passes the embedded struct drm_device
  └─ i915_drm_suspend(dev)
       dev_priv = to_i915(dev)
       reconstructs the same struct drm_i915_private *
       display = dev_priv->display
  └─ intel_display_driver_suspend(display)
       passes struct intel_display *
```

Relevant assignments:

```c
/* i915_pm_suspend(), :1394 and :1404 */
struct drm_i915_private *i915 = kdev_to_i915(kdev);
return i915_drm_suspend(&i915->drm);

/* i915_drm_suspend(), :1105–1106 */
struct drm_i915_private *dev_priv = to_i915(dev);
struct intel_display *display = dev_priv->display;

/* :1120 */
intel_display_driver_suspend(display);
```

So `dev_priv` is not passed directly into the display suspend function. It flows through the embedded DRM device:

```text
struct device *kdev
  → kdev_to_i915()
  → struct drm_i915_private *i915
  → &i915->drm
  → to_i915(dev)
  → struct drm_i915_private *dev_priv
  → dev_priv->display
  → struct intel_display *display
  → intel_display_driver_suspend(display)
```

At `drivers/gpu/drm/i915/display/intel_display_driver.c:684–706`, `intel_display_driver_suspend()` uses `display->drm` and calls `drm_atomic_helper_suspend(display->drm)`.
